To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) MRI can detect human T cells in canine brain at concentrations of Gd sufficient for clinical application; 2) MRI contrast is related to the binding of Gd to the T cells; and 3) MRI can distinguish human from bovine T cells in canine brains.
MRI can be used to image Gd-labeled monoclonals directed at human T cells implanted in canine brains.
MRI can be used to detect and localize cells in vivo by coupling them to Gd-DPTA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of MRI to detect the distribution of cells in the central nervous system.
the development of MRI contrast agents for the detection of implanted human T lymphocytes in the brain of dogs.
developing a new method to detect implanted human cells in the brain with MRI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Gd-labeled murine monoclonals can be used to detect human T cells implanted in the brain of canine models and can be differentiated from canine T cells implanted in canine brains.
MRI is a sensitive technique to detect human T lymphocytes within canine brain.
MRI can detect human T cells implanted in canine brains with Gd-labeled murine monoclonial antibodies directed at human T cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MRI can be used to image human T cells implanted in the brain of dogs.
Gd-labeled monoclonals can be used for MRI of implanted human T cells in canine brain.
MRI can detect the presence of human T cells in canine brain and distinguish them from bovine T cells implanted in the brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MRI contrast of Gd-labeled monoclonals directed against human T cell implants in canine brain can be used to detect the presence of the implanted cells.
Gd-DTPAs coupled to monoclonal antibodies directed against human T lymphocyte cell surface markers can be detected in vivo by magnetic resonance imaging.
Gd-labeled antibody polymers can be used to image implanted human T lymphocyte tumors in canine brain.
